body:
Rust keeps modules and functions in separate namespaces, so `mod merge;` next to `fn merge` is valid Rust. But `language::rust.Cx::duplicates` treats them as one name and refuses the file (`merge is defined twice in extract::rust`).

`submit` saved this pair anyway in run 1eb9fa406ebb94eb of task:ea673350c54b241e. After that, writing the crate back from the store failed, and two tests broke: `every_file_of_this_crate_joins_back_exactly` and `a_copy_of_this_crate_is_imported_and_written_back_exactly`. So `submit` and the importer disagree about the same code.

### Change
- `duplicates` counts a `mod` as a clash only with another type-namespace item (struct, enum, union, trait, type, mod), not with a fn, const or static.

### Done when
- A test shows that `fn f` and `mod f` in one module import and write back exactly.
- The existing `the_same_name_twice_is_refused` cases still pass.
- `test --all --project solace-cli` passes.
title: rust: a module may share a function's name
